title: "Chapter 4 · Context & Ritual Psychology"

{{< include ../../_includes/lang-switcher/module-04.en.qmd >}}

Chemistry explains why a leaf can wake you. History explains why that leaf is cheap in your cupboard. This chapter asks what else rides along in the mug: **warmth**, **ritual**, and **expectation**.

Hold three kitchen pictures. A cozy mug in the hand while you meet someone new. A short, familiar brew sequence—measure, watch, wait—before a hard task. A label or vessel that says "specialty" versus "just bag." Same compounds can share the cup with all three. Effects are tints, not destiny—and replication humility stays on the page.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Words to know on this journey"}
- **Anterior insular cortex** — brain area that handles both body temperature and feelings like trust or empathy.
- **Embodied cognition** — the claim that body feelings (like warmth) can shape social judgments.
- **Error-related negativity (ERN)** — a quick brain "oops" signal after mistakes; predictable rituals can blunt related anxiety responses in some studies.
- **Expectation / label cues** — belief about what the drink is, shaped by price, packaging, vessel, or story.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
**Read the story; open More detail boxes only when curious.** Context scenes stay open; denser lab tables live in foldouts.

## Carry-forward into Decisions

If you take only one sentence into [Chapter 5](../module-05/index.qmd), take this: **context is part of the dose.** Temperature, ritual, and expectation ride along with caffeine and [L-theanine](../../glossary.qmd#l-theanine). That is why careful decision studies lock mug temperature and bitterness—and why a headline that ignores them is incomplete.
